subject: Data retention exception follow-up - Acme Health
messages:
From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today - data retention + PII handling

Thanks for the call this morning, Rafael — good to meet the team. A quick recap from our side and the specific asks I want to capture so we can move toward procurement: 

- Acme Health is evaluating Redwood for our patient-facing assistant (PHI scope). Main asks from clinical and security: 
  - Zero retention (0-retention) for payloads that may contain PII/PHI (request/response content) — we need written confirmation that these payloads will not be stored persistently.
  - Short-term / shortened logs for telemetry only (7 days max) and aggregated where possible. No identifiable data in logs.
  - Data residency: US-only hosting and key management.
  - SOC 2 evidence and any privacy-by-design notes.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 0-retention exception for request/response payloads for a pilot, and what controls you would apply (redaction/tokenization, KMS, audit logs)? Procurement will need: a short SOW/addendum and DocuSign-ready contract language.

Next steps: please loop in legal/security and share proposed language. Happy to schedule a short follow-up on Thursday if that helps.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Johnson
Director, Information Security
Acme Health
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com, John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today - data retention + PII handling

Sarah — really appreciate the clear recap. Short answer: we can support a pilot with strong protections, but there are a few legal/operational guardrails we'll want to align on. I attached a proposed retention exception doc that outlines options and tradeoffs (proposed-retention-exception.docx).

High level from product/sales:
- Payloads (request/response) can be configured to not persist outside the inference path. We can disable KV caching and ingestion logging for the pilot.
- For audit and reliability, we typically keep minimal telemetry; we can aggregate and truncate to meet the 7-day requirement.
- Data residency: we can host in US regions and use customer-managed KMS where required.

I'm looping in Marissa (legal) and Camila (security) to propose the specific language/procedures. Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood shares a 1-page addendum for the pilot (we've attached a template).
2) Security/engineering run a short tech feasibility review — we can schedule a call Wednesday.
3) Procurement to confirm SOW items and routing for DocuSign.

Is Thursday at 10am PT a good time for a 30-minute follow-up?

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today - data retention + PII handling

Thanks for the summary, Sarah — and thanks for looping me in, Rafael. A few legal points to set expectations before we draft addendum language: 

- Absolute 0-retention for all logs is operationally risky and, in some cases, conflicts with required audit/auditability obligations — we rarely do blanket permanent deletions of audit trails. That said, we can scope a narrow exception for payloads (request/response content) for a defined pilot period with documented controls and compensating measures.

- Typical approach we recommend and can contractually commit to for a pilot:
  1) Non-persistent payload handling: payloads will not be written to long-term storage; any ephemeral buffers used for inference will be cleared immediately after the request completes.
  2) PII redaction/transform: where possible, apply on-ingest redaction or tokenization to remove direct identifiers before any optional logging. This is a configuration/engineering task we can scope for the pilot.
  3) Minimal audit metadata: we can retain non-identifying audit metadata (request id, timestamp, model version) for a limited window (we typically propose 7 days) to support incident investigation.
  4) Data residency and KMS: include clause requiring US region hosting and option for customer-managed keys.

- We will draft pilot addendum language that: (a) defines the scope and duration of the 0-retention pilot, (b) specifies what is redacted, (c) defines telemetry retained and retention window, and (d) enumerates acceptance criteria (QA checks and one security review). Template attached: retention-policy-template.docx.

If Acme agrees to the above approach we can prepare an SOW + addendum and route to DocuSign. Rafael — happy to review the final language before it goes to Acme.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today - data retention + PII handling

On Tue, Mar 16, 2026 at 9:12 AM Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 0-retention exception for request/response payloads for a pilot, and what controls you would apply (redaction/tokenization, KMS, audit logs)?

Hi Sarah — quick security/engineering notes on feasibility: 
- Feasible: we can configure isolated inference endpoints that do not write request/response payloads to persistent logs. This requires: disabling KV cache, disabling ingestion logging, and prohibiting async request dumps.
- Compensating controls we propose:
  * On-ingest redaction rules (regex-based + optional model-assisted PII scrub) applied before any optional downstream recording.
  * Customer-managed KMS keys for any short-lived encryption of ephemeral artifacts (if requested).
  * Aggregated telemetry only: we can emit aggregated metrics (request counts, 5xx/latency aggregates) to monitoring systems and retain them for 7 days. No full-text payload in telemetry.
- Note: disabling logs limits our ability to do root-cause debugging for rare incidents. For the pilot we request a joint acceptance test and a temporary debug process (time-limited, logged, and with explicit approvals) if needed.

I've attached our SOC2 summary for Acme's security review (SOC2_summary.pdf). From an engineering standpoint we can deliver the pilot within a ~3-week window after SOW/signature to implement the configuration and run the acceptance tests.

Happy to run a 30-minute technical deep-dive with your engineers this week.

— Camila Reyes
Head of Security & Trust Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, John Lee <john.lee@acmehealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today - data retention + PII handling

Thanks Rafael/Marissa/Camila — this is exactly what we needed to see. Acme agrees to proceed with the pilot under the scope you outlined: 0-retention for payloads, 7-day aggregated telemetry, US-only hosting, customer KMS option, and joint acceptance testing.

Procurement — please confirm the SOW items below and prepare the DocuSign routing:
- Pilot length: 60 days
- Deliverables: configured endpoint, redaction rules applied, acceptance test checklist
- SLA/rollback: documentation on how to revert to standard logging in case of operational needs

Rafael — please send the SOW/addendum and a DocuSign link when ready. Camila — let’s book the technical deep-dive Thursday 10am PT (per Rafael's suggestion).

Thanks all, looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Information Security
Acme Health
